narrative.overview: Luxury real estate developer energy applied to a Southwest Florida remodeling contractor. The same confidence that sells estates in Naples, now representing the team that builds the kitchens inside them. Warm darkness, heavy serif headlines, editorial pacing. The brand doesn't explain itself, because it doesn't need to.
narrative.sectionRhythm: The system moves between two modes: cinematic dark sections (ink backgrounds, warm-white type, terracotta Reserve accent) and editorial light sections (plaster-white or warm-linen grounds, ink type, structured columns). The transition between them creates the page's rhythm. Never three dark sections in a row; never three light sections in a row.
narrative.antiReferences: This system explicitly rejects: the generic contractor site with stock hard-hat photography and blue-orange gradients; the Houzz-style review grid where everything is a thumbnail; the SaaS startup with purple glows and animated counters; and the interior design portfolio that converts nobody because it prioritizes precious aesthetics over trust.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-to-light alternating section rhythm — cinematic depth without monotony
Pill-shaped controls at every interaction surface (buttons, tags, avatars, progress fills)
Playfair Display italic as the emotional register; DM Sans uppercase spaced label as the structural register
Terracotta Reserve as the only warm accent — used sparingly so its presence is decisive
Credentials (license number, named contractors, project count) treated as design elements, not legal boilerplate

namedRules.oneReserveRule: Terracotta Reserve appears on no more than 10% of any given screen surface. It is never used as a section background, never used in display headlines. It earns attention through constraint. Every second appearance diminishes the first.
namedRules.noPureValuesRule: #000000 and #ffffff are prohibited. Ink and Plaster White are the functional equivalents — both warm-shifted enough to feel chosen, not defaulted.
namedRules.italicSecondLineRule: Display and Headline H1/H2s frequently split with the second line in Playfair Display italic. This is structural, not decorative — it signals the emotional clause vs. the factual clause. Never apply italic to full headlines; always reserve it for the trailing modifier.
namedRules.eyebrowRule: Every section starts with a label in the DM Sans uppercase spaced style (Driftwood, 11px, tracking 0.3em) before the headline. No section headline is permitted to appear without its eyebrow.
namedRules.flatByDefaultRule: No shadow appears at rest on any component except card-light. Shadows are reserved for state (nav scroll, hover on interactive elements) and structural separation (sticky nav).
namedRules.noBlurRule: Backdrop-filter blur is used in one place: dark translucent form card panels layered over section backgrounds. Never use blur on cards, buttons, or inline UI.

dos: Alternate dark and light sections. The rhythm of Ink-to-Plaster-White is how this system creates depth without shadows.
Pair every headline with an eyebrow label. DM Sans, 0.6875rem, uppercase, tracking 0.3em, Driftwood.
Split display headlines with an italic second line in Playfair Display.
Use Terracotta Reserve sparingly. Hover states, credential check icons, blog category labels.
Keep buttons pill-shaped at every scale. border-radius 9999px on all interactive controls.
Treat trust signals (FL License #CBC1269972, named contractors, project counts) as design elements.
Use Plaster White, not pure white, for light backgrounds. #faf7f4 not #ffffff.
Cap body text at 65-75ch line length.
donts: Don't use Terracotta Reserve as a section background fill or in display headlines.
Don't use generic contractor site patterns: stock photos of hard hats, blue or orange gradients.
Don't build a Houzz-style review grid or comparison-shopping layout.
Don't add SaaS-style CTAs: purple gradients, glowing buttons, animated counters.
Don't over-style to the point of not converting — the interior design portfolio trap.
Don't use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe.
Don't add shadows to flat-by-default components.
Don't use DM Sans for display headlines, or Playfair Display for body paragraphs.
